To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
technological unemployment and human dis-enhancement are real problems, and that the former is a consequence of the latter.
the ICT sector, in the last decade, has been a cause of human disenhancement and that the current trend in the ICT sector is to increase human disenhancement.
the use of robots and AI is not only a threat to the future of work but also a threat to human flourishing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the moral assessment of technological innovations, and in particular of those that are likely to cause a decrease of human abilities and expectations.
the following questions: What is human disenhancement?
the moral evaluation of technological innovations that are not directly related to human enhancement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
technological unemployment is a moral issue, and that the current technological innovation is a moral problem.
the ICT sector is morally problematic because it is responsible for human disenhancement, which in turn causes the disappearance of middle-class jobs.
the ICT sector is not a moral duty for the state, and it is not a moral right for the private sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technological unemployment is a form of human disenhancement.
the moral problem with automation is that it disenhances the human race as a whole, and not that it disenhanced a particular group of people, such as the middle class.

, in the long run, technological innovation in the computer sector can be morally objectionable, if it is not accompanied by the development of other technologies, which would enhance the skills of the people who would be made unemployed by the computer-driven automation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to avoid the risk of human disenhancement, we need to develop a new ethics of technological innovation.

, when assessing the moral value of a technological innovation, it is necessary to consider not only its local and immediate effect, but also its long-term and global consequences, including the effects that are not immediately visible, but that will be produced in the future.
technological innovation is morally relevant, even when it is not directly related to biomedical enhancement.
